title: The Unnameable Return
goal: Return the lazy pipeline itself — its true type can't be written, but it can be promised.
hints: The filter's real type involves a closure — a type with no name you could write.
impl Trait says: 'a concrete type exists, it does Iterator, and only I know which one'.
explanation: The pipeline's true type is Filter<Range<i32>, {closure}> — unwritable because closures have anonymous types. `impl Iterator<Item = i32>` is the tool for exactly this: a static, concrete, zero-cost return whose name stays private. A bare trait as a return type is unsized and rejected outright, and Vec<i32> demands a .collect() the body never does — it would also throw away the laziness the caller might want. impl Trait keeps pipelines composable across function boundaries.

source.attribution: inspired by iterators and impl-Trait patterns
